operations.name: limit_function_type_contract.md
operations.content:
---
description: p-limit limitFunction: PromiseLike fn + Options in, Promise fn exposing clearQueue and onIdle (type-level)
type: project
---
In the p-limit project at /work/p-limit, the public contract of the exported `limitFunction` is its declaration in `index.d.ts`: `function_` must be `(...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>` and `options` is the `Options` object. Its return type was changed in this slice from `((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>` to `((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>`, and `LimitFunction` now declares `onIdle: () => Promise<void>;`.

Contrast preserved from the same inspected declaration: the `LimitFunction` call signature takes `function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`, so a synchronous return is declared acceptable for `limit(...)` input while `limitFunction`'s input is PromiseLike-only.

All of the above is a type-level restriction read from the declaration, not proof of runtime enforcement. Keep the Promise/PromiseLike distinction: the input is `PromiseLike<ReturnType>`, the output function returns `Promise<ReturnType>`. The declaration by itself does not establish that any named test ran or passed.

evidence.quote:
<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(
		function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType,

-): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;
+): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>;

newMemories.name: limiter_onidle_contract.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit index.js treats the limiter as idle only when activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0
---
In the p-limit project at /work/p-limit, the `onIdle()` support added to `index.js` defines idleness as `const isIdle = () => activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0;`, so a job that merely occupies a reserved slot (activeCount incremented in `resumeNext`) keeps the limiter non-idle, as does any still-queued item. Waiters are stored with `idleWaiters.unshift(resolve)` and released in FIFO order by `checkIdle()` via `idleWaiters.pop()()`. `onIdle()` returns `Promise.resolve()` when the limiter is already idle.

`clearQueue()` in the `rejectOnClear: false` branch calls `queue.clear()` and then `checkIdle()`: the discarded promises remain unresolved, but they no longer occupy the queue, so they do not keep the limiter non-idle. An ad-hoc `node` probe on a `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: false})` whose single slot was still occupied printed `pending after clear 0 active 1` followed by `result: still pending` — the `onIdle()` waiter was released only after the running job settled, not by `clearQueue()` alone.

This is implementation behavior read from the edited source plus ad-hoc probes; it is not a test-suite verification of a general guarantee. The corresponding public declaration is `onIdle: () => Promise<void>;` on `LimitFunction` in `index.d.ts`.

evidence.quote:
pending after clear 0 active 1
result: still pending
